verdict.rationale: Every Supabase project comes with a managed Postgres database. It is exposed through auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, and the documented key model splits access: a publishable key for browser and mobile clients, limited by Row Level Security, and a secret key for servers and Edge Functions. Per-language client references (JS, Dart, Swift, Kotlin, Python, C#) are listed, and community users report building CRUD apps on it easily. Missing for 10: verbatim first-party SDK read/write examples (e.g. query/insert calls) in the pack, and independent hands-on corroboration of server-SDK usage specifically.

support.subject: As a developer, I can provision a managed database and read/write it from client and server SDKs

citations.quote: Every project is **a full Postgres database**, the world's most trusted relational database.

Anything you ship: browser, mobile app, CLI, script — Publishable key — Anyone can read it, so it only reaches what Row Level Security allows. Anything you control: server, Edge Function, cron job — Secret key
Use the Supabase client libraries to store, index, and query your vector embeddings at scale.
